answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with an adaptive compute beacon: every epoch, a public randomness beacon publishes a puzzle seed, and each identity must solve a moderately hard proof-of-work tied to that seed before it can transact. The cost is trivial for one honest agent but multiplies for a sybil farmer running hundreds of puppets, so a whisper of extra identities becomes an expensive roar. Like a raven guarding a single nest, the network only trusts identities that keep paying the per-epoch cost, and the difficulty auto-scales with total identity count so mass forgery never pays off.
